skill.name: gene-database
skill.description: Query NCBI Gene with E-utilities and Datasets APIs for gene search, metadata retrieval, batch lookup, and annotation workflows.
skill.summary: Search and retrieve NCBI Gene records for bioinformatics annotation workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The executable scripts make intended outbound requests to NCBI Gene APIs and one batch workflow can write results to a user-selected file. API-key and command-execution alerts are false positives from parameter names, placeholders, and Markdown examples; no hardcoded secrets, environment access, prompt injection, or hidden system reconnaissance was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound requests send gene queries to NCBI services.
remediation.suggestion: Document that gene IDs, symbols, organisms, and optional API keys are sent to NCBI, and add request timeouts to every urllib call.

remediation.issue: The batch output path is user controlled and opened for writing.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse overwrites by default, resolve output paths safely, or require confirmation before writing outside the working directory.

remediation.issue: NCBI API keys can be passed on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Support a secure prompt or documented environment variable so users can avoid placing real keys in shell history.

remediation.issue: Datasets API path segments are built from user input.
remediation.suggestion: URL-encode gene symbols, taxon values, and gene IDs before constructing Datasets API paths.

content.value_statement: Gene lookup often requires several NCBI endpoints and careful query formatting. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable workflows for gene search, retrieval, and batch annotation.
actual_capabilities: Search NCBI Gene by symbol, name, disease term, chromosome, organism, or Gene ID.
Retrieve gene summaries through ESearch, ESummary, EFetch, and NCBI Datasets API workflows.
Batch lookup gene symbols or Gene IDs and export structured annotation results.
Resolve common organism names to NCBI taxon IDs for Datasets API requests.
Guide users through disease, pathway, variant, publication, and cross-species gene workflows.
Show examples for JSON, XML, text, and human-readable gene output.
limitations: Requires internet access to NCBI services for live data retrieval.
NCBI rate limits apply, especially when no API key is provided.
Returned annotations depend on current NCBI records and may change over time.
Does not perform downstream statistical analysis, sequence alignment, or clinical interpretation.

use_cases.title: Annotate a Gene Panel
use_cases.description: Map a list of gene symbols to Gene IDs, descriptions, organisms, chromosomes, and map locations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Queries
use_cases.description: Build precise NCBI Gene searches for diseases, pathways, phenotypes, publications, and model organisms.

use_cases.title: Check Gene Metadata
use_cases.description: Retrieve current NCBI summaries for single genes before writing reports, tickets, or documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Gene by Symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to search NCBI Gene for BRCA1 in human. Return the Gene ID, official symbol, description, organism, chromosome, and map location.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Gene Details
prompt_templates.scenario: Get a detailed record for a known Gene ID.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to fetch NCBI Gene ID 672. Summarize nomenclature, aliases, organism, genomic location, transcripts, and available output formats.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Annotate Genes
prompt_templates.scenario: Process a small research gene list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to annotate BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS for human. Produce a concise table with Gene ID, description, chromosome, and status.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Disease Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced query planning across NCBI Gene workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to design an NCBI Gene workflow for finding human genes linked to diabetes, retrieving summaries, checking publications, and avoiding rate-limit problems.

output_examples.output: A concise result with Gene ID 672, symbol BRCA1, the official description, human organism details, chromosome 17, and map location.

output_examples.input: Annotate a list of four cancer genes.
output_examples.output: A table-style summary showing each query symbol, matched Gene ID, description, organism, chromosome, map location, and not-found status when needed.

output_examples.input: Plan a pathway gene search for apoptosis.
output_examples.output: A workflow that searches by Gene Ontology term, limits results by organism, retrieves summaries in batches, and records the exact query terms used.

best_practices: Always include an organism or taxon filter when searching by gene symbol.
Use Gene IDs for exact retrieval when a trusted identifier is available.
Batch requests and respect NCBI rate limits to avoid failed lookups.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a gene symbol is unique across species.
Do not paste real API keys into shared prompts, logs, or examples.
Do not use returned gene annotations as clinical guidance without expert review.

faq.question: Which NCBI services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses E-utilities for search and summaries, plus the NCBI Datasets API for gene metadata retrieval.

faq.question: Does it require an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it increases NCBI rate limits for larger workflows.

faq.question: Can it process multiple genes at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script accepts comma-separated Gene IDs or a file of gene symbols.

faq.question: Can it return sequence data?
faq.answer: It can request formats such as XML, text, GenBank, or FASTA when supported by the selected NCBI endpoint.

faq.question: Is the data stored locally?
faq.answer: Most scripts print results to the console. The batch workflow can write a JSON output file when a path is provided.

faq.question: Can it interpret clinical variants?
faq.answer: No. It can help find gene and variant-related records, but clinical interpretation requires qualified review.
